regions.full_page: My Dear Niece Dorothy: - God bless you this dear, beautiful Feast of the most priviliged Spouse of Mary. May be too be watching over you and yours! I've been wanting to write you these many months. Indeed you have been on my mind quite a little ever since that memorable day we conclude with you and your little family on the "mount" in view of the majestic "old Ranier. Who would believe that nearly three years has passed since that day? How many more-times three, till we follow so many of our dear ones gone ahead of that land-mark event, and join even those who have followed since? -- poor, dear Brother Guss, (at least for me), one of the notables. I would like to continue playing with memories but time forbids me to waste it on events that have passed and do pass like soap-bubles, no matter how grand and gaudy, unless they pertain to the one thing necessary - knowing God better so as to love Him and serve Him better and save our immortal souls. For who can fully appreciate the privilege that Almighty God has given each one of us in just this possibility of our helping Him in the work of Redemption and thus saving our own "destiny for eternal glory?" "0, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God!" You will be wondering what all this may be coming to; and there is so much that I would write you that a whole book would not exhaust it. So much, when I think of your dear Mother, Sister Nell or Ellie, as we used to call her in her mother-like efforts to make the rest of us contented and happy in the long decads back in our family history, in Prescott, in Trimbelle, in St. Croix Co. in Superior, Wis. I think you must have been the baby when she - your dear Mother - wrote that notable letter describing the 500 mile-trip to Christmas Mass, that I gave you last Nov- ember. At all events I wanted to have a heart-to-heart talk with you on that occasion but the shortness of your stay and circumstances made that impracticable for what I felt you and poor, dear Charlie needed. I could see from the start that he had something on his mind. He could not resis- Lamenting it in a little personal interview we had together. I'd never met Charlie before that refered-day on the Mouth and then a day or two afterwards out at aurelia's place on Lake Washington and I surely felt like congratulating you on such a husband and on the blessing God had be- stowed on your union - such dear children.
